A1.justification: Both PDFs describe NovelQA and retain matching dataset definitions and experiments. All 18 pages of v1 and 22 pages of v2, including appendices and visual material, support comparison. Internal labeling inconsistencies do not prevent identifying the substantive changes.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B report original model evaluations, question-type and position analyses, closed-book tests, evidence-recall results, and evaluator-agreement measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and additionally reports Claude 3 Sonnet performance, human-reader accuracy, and aggregated evidence-position results.

M1.justification: The two-stage annotation approach, QA formulation, prompting, and GPT-4-based evaluation remain. The shortened table of selected templates and expanded descriptions of manual checking do not establish a changed construction procedure or a new algorithm or model.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same 2,305-question English-novel benchmark, with identical complexity and aspect counts in v1 Table 1 and v2 Table 6. v2 newly documents the public-domain/copyrighted composition; its human study uses existing NovelQA questions. No additional dataset, language, domain, or QA task is established.

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 adds Claude 3 Sonnet to the four models in v1 Table 2, and Section 4.1 adds human-reader performance. Claude 3 is absent from the detailed question-type, closed-book, and evidence-recall comparisons. Gemini 1.5 is reported only as an unsuccessful attempt, without comparative accuracy.

E3.justification: v2 reports a new human-evaluation protocol covering 100 questions from five novels, with generative answers preceding multiple-choice answers and readers answering novels they had not annotated. Existing model truncation, question batching, temperature, and grading settings remain. Template-design pretests are now described using Claude 2.1 instead of Claude2-100K, without establishing that they were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 Table 10 extends the evidence-position analysis with aggregate pre-/post-100K accuracies and weighted averages. The question-type breakdowns, length-stratified plots, representative errors, closed-book test, and evidence-recall analysis are retained. Moving the closed-book analysis to Appendix E.5 does not constitute its removal.

E5.justification: The 100-case annotation-agreement study and 800-output human/GPT-4 agreement study already appear in v1. Their Kappa methodology and evaluator-agreement table are retained. v2 expands procedural descriptions without adding repeated-run reporting, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: v2 adds Claude 3 Sonnet scores of 71.11% multiple-choice and 53.66% generative accuracy, plus human scores of 97% and 90% on a 100-question subset. Original aggregate model scores remain unchanged. Other additions include Table 10's position aggregates and Gemini generation failures on 816 questions. Figure 5 revises the minimum input length from 67,546 to 65,876 and adds a public-domain distribution. Detailed multiple-choice score blocks are retained but inconsistently relabeled across v1 Table 10 and v2 Table 11, preventing their interpretation as verified performance changes.

T1.justification: The data-record definitions and mathematical QA formulation in Section 3.1 remain unchanged. Neither version provides a theoretical development or proof that changes between versions. v2's question-to-ability mapping is conceptual rather than formal.

C1.justification: v2 removes the explicit claim to be the first long-range QA dataset within computational literary studies and reduces that contribution's prominence in the conclusion. It foregrounds documents averaging over 200K tokens, a property already claimed in v1. The central manually annotated benchmark and model-difficulty claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 relates its interpretation of model difficulty to the new human-reader comparison and explicitly maps question types to retrieval, integration, summarization, and reasoning abilities in Table 8. Existing interpretations of position effects, memorization, and errors remain, as do the English-language, API-access, and hardware limitations.

D1.justification: v2 adds public-domain/copyrighted book and question counts, Apache-2.0 licensing and release boundaries, separate leaderboard coverage, and the tokenizer used for length statistics. Annotation documentation now specifies recruitment, edition consistency, typical questions per novel, three-author review, distractor checking, and approximately $3,500 total cost. These expand documentation; existing hardware and prompt specifications largely remain.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds a contrast with Needle in a Haystack and citations to Counting-Stars and LongICLBench, supported by the new benchmark-feature comparison in Figure 4. The computational-literary-studies subsection and associated references, including BookSum and BooookScore, are removed. The long-context-modeling discussion is retained in Appendix C.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the narrative: it changes the title and author information, rewrites and expands the annotation account, relocates modeling-related work and limitations, and moves closed-book analysis into expanded appendices. The previous two-appendix organization becomes Appendices A–E, with revised subsection structure and explanations.

P2.justification: The document switches from two-column to single-column presentation. Figure 2 is redrawn with a replacement example; absolute and relative position plots are merged; detailed model tables become two-by-two panels; and Figure 5 gains a public-domain panel. New benchmark-comparison, question-ability, and position-summary displays further change the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: The human evaluation supplies an answerability reference absent from v1, while clearer annotation, licensing, and access information improves the benchmark's usability. Updated model coverage and position summaries add useful evidence. These gains are limited by unresolved table-label problems and the retained GPT-4-best claim despite Claude 3's higher generative score. Overall, the additional validation and documentation provide a modest net improvement.
